lines: {target}? Sound itself can <shake>wake trouble</shake>. I would write the warning down first.
If anyone heads for Ancient City, tell them: <pulse>Step softly</pulse> and leave the shiny things alone. I will be at the lectern.
Sculk does not need eyes to notice you. I will write that warning down.
Ancient City is no small story. Old stories usually leave out the screams.
I will remember Ancient City as a city where <pulse>silence matters</pulse> more than armor. I will write the warning larger than the wonder.
{target}? Old gold still has guards. I would write the warning down first.
If anyone heads for Bastion Remnant, tell them: Do not touch <color:gold>gold</color> unless you are ready for angry piglins. I will be at the lectern.
Blackstone halls do not forgive greed. I will write that warning down.
Bastion Remnant is no small story. Old stories usually leave out the screams.
I will remember Bastion Remnant as a broken stronghold where greed still has teeth. I will write the warning larger than the wonder.
{target}? Treasure makes people dig past good sense. I would write the warning down first.
If anyone heads for Buried Treasure, tell them: Watch the <wavy>tide</wavy> and the shovel both. I will be at the lectern.
Sand hides holes as well as chests. I will write that warning down.
Buried Treasure is no small story. Old stories usually leave out the screams.
I will remember Buried Treasure as a chest under sand that can make friends argue. I will write the warning larger than the wonder.
{target}? Sandstone can hide a trap under your feet. I would write the warning down first.
If anyone heads for Desert Pyramid, tell them: Break floors carefully and listen before stepping down. I will be at the lectern.
Old pressure plates wait patiently. I will write that warning down.
Desert Pyramid is no small story. Old stories usually leave out the screams.
I will remember Desert Pyramid as a quiet pyramid with a loud mistake under it. I will write the warning larger than the wonder.
{target}? The sky is open and the ground is not always there. I would write the warning down first.
If anyone heads for End City, tell them: Watch every <shake>bridge</shake> and every shulker box. I will be at the lectern.
Purple towers make falling feel too easy. I will write that warning down.
End City is no small story. Old stories usually leave out the screams.
I will remember End City as a tall city built where home feels very far away. I will write the warning larger than the wonder.
{target}? Bridges hang over lava and worse things patrol them. I would write the warning down first.
If anyone heads for Nether Fortress, tell them: Keep <color:red>fire protection</color> close and pride far away. I will be at the lectern.
Blazes turn hallways into ovens. I will write that warning down.
Nether Fortress is no small story. Old stories usually leave out the screams.
I will remember Nether Fortress as a black bridge where the air itself wants a fight. I will write the warning larger than the wonder.
{target}? A little shelter can keep a strange secret below. I would write the warning down first.
If anyone heads for Igloo, tell them: Check the trapdoor before trusting the bed. I will be at the lectern.
Snow can cover kindness and trouble both. I will write that warning down.
Igloo is no small story. Old stories usually leave out the screams.
I will remember Igloo as a small white house with more beneath it than above it. I will write the warning larger than the wonder.
{target}? Vines and stone hide tripwires well. I would write the warning down first.
If anyone heads for Jungle Pyramid, tell them: Move slow and keep hands off strange levers. I will be at the lectern.
Mossy stone is good at pretending nothing happened. I will write that warning down.
Jungle Pyramid is no small story. Old stories usually leave out the screams.
I will remember Jungle Pyramid as a jungle ruin that waits with string pulled tight. I will write the warning larger than the wonder.
{target}? Old supports and cave spiders both like the dark. I would write the warning down first.
If anyone heads for Mineshaft, tell them: Mind the webs and never trust quiet rails. I will be at the lectern.
Wood below ground means someone left in a hurry. I will write that warning down.
Mineshaft is no small story. Old stories usually leave out the screams.
I will remember Mineshaft as a tunnel where every beam sounds tired. I will write the warning larger than the wonder.
{target}? Gold country draws danger underground. I would write the warning down first.

{target}? Guardians watch the water from every side. I would write the warning down first.
If anyone heads for Ocean Monument, tell them: Bring milk, doors, and enough air to regret nothing. I will be at the lectern.

Ocean Monument is no small story. Old stories usually leave out the screams.
I will remember Ocean Monument as a drowned temple with eyes in the walls. I will write the warning larger than the wonder.
{target}? Even old bones can sit in bad air. I would write the warning down first.

{target}? Warm water can still hide drowned trouble. I would write the warning down first.

{target}? Banners mean <shake>crossbows</shake> are near. I would write the warning down first.

{target}? Broken obsidian still remembers the Nether. I would write the warning down first.

I will remember Ruined Portal as a broken doorway that still points somewhere bad. I will write the warning larger than the wonder.
{target}? Nether heat and desert heat make poor company. I would write the warning down first.
